content: Anthropic, known for creating the AI platform Claude, was the target of a 2025 class-action lawsuit that resulted in the largest copyright settlement to date. While it was determined that Anthropic could use fairly obtained books to train large language models (LLMs) for Claude, the company resorted to using pirate libraries with thousands of unauthorized copies. This was later deemed an unfair use of authors' copyrighted work. Anthropic agreed to a settlement of $1.5 billion to be distributed among the publishers and authors of approximately half a million books.
